nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states over a nonempty alphabet. If $A$ accepts some infinite word, then there are finite words $u$ and $v$ with $v$ nonempty such that $A$ accepts the ultimately periodic word $u v^\omega = u v v v \cdots$.
nodes.title: Nonempty Büchi languages contain ultimately periodic words

nodes.summary: For states $s$ and $t$ of a nondeterministic Büchi automaton, the automaton can move from $s$ to $t$ by reading some finite word (possibly empty) if and only if $t$ is reachable from $s$ in zero or more steps of the transition graph, which has an edge from $p$ to $q$ when some symbol takes $p$ to $q$.
nodes.title: Reachability by words is reachability in the transition graph

nodes.summary: For states $s$ and $t$ of a nondeterministic Büchi automaton, the automaton can move from $s$ to $t$ by reading some nonempty finite word if and only if $t$ is reachable from $s$ in one or more steps of the transition graph, which has an edge from $p$ to $q$ when some symbol takes $p$ to $q$.
nodes.title: Nonempty words and paths of positive length

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states and finitely many symbols, with decidable equality of states, and whose transitions, start states and accepting states are decidable. Then $A$ has a lasso if and only if its set of lasso states, computed by finite reachability closures as the accepting states that are reachable from a start state and lie on a nonempty cycle, is nonempty.
nodes.title: Lasso detection by finite reachability

nodes.summary: A nondeterministic Büchi automaton has a lasso if and only if there are a start state $s_0$ and an accepting state $s$ such that $s$ is reachable from $s_0$ in zero or more steps of the transition graph and $s$ is reachable from itself in one or more steps; the transition graph has an edge from $p$ to $q$ when some symbol takes $p$ to $q$.
nodes.title: The lasso condition in the transition graph

nodes.summary: If a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states accepts some infinite word, then it has a lasso: some accepting state is visited twice along an accepting run, and the run between the two visits is the cycle.
nodes.title: An accepted word yields a lasso

nodes.summary: A nondeterministic Büchi automaton has a lasso if there are a start state $s_0$ and an accepting state $s$ such that the automaton can move from $s_0$ to $s$ by reading some finite word $u$, and from $s$ back to $s$ by reading some nonempty finite word $v$.
nodes.title: Lasso of a Büchi automaton

nodes.summary: For a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states and finitely many symbols, with decidable equality of states, and whose transitions, start states and accepting states are decidable, the emptiness test returns true if and only if the automaton accepts no infinite word.
nodes.title: Correctness of the Büchi emptiness test

nodes.summary: For a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states and finitely many symbols, with decidable equality of states, and whose transitions, start states and accepting states are decidable, the emptiness test returns true exactly when the automaton has no lasso. It decides this by computing the set of lasso states; by the lasso characterization, it returns true iff no infinite word is accepted.
nodes.title: Büchi emptiness test

nodes.summary: For finitely many states, the language of a nondeterministic Büchi automaton is nonempty iff some accepting state is reachable from a start state and lies on a nonempty cycle.
nodes.title: Lasso characterization of Büchi nonemptiness

nodes.summary: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a nondeterministic Büchi automaton over a nonempty alphabet. Suppose $s_0$ is a start state and $s$ an accepting state of $\mathcal{A}$, that reading the finite word $u$ the automaton can move from $s_0$ to $s$, and that reading a nonempty finite word $v$ it can move from $s$ back to $s$. Then $\mathcal{A}$ accepts the infinite word $u v^\omega = u v v v \cdots$.
nodes.title: Lassos give accepted ultimately periodic words

nodes.summary: For a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states, decidable equality of states, a finite alphabet, and decidable transitions, start set and accepting set, the lasso states form the finite set of accepting states $s$ that are reachable from some start state in zero or more transitions and lie on a nonempty cycle, that is, $s$ is reachable from itself in one or more transitions.
nodes.title: Lasso states of a finite Büchi automaton

nodes.summary: A nondeterministic Büchi automaton accepts an infinite word $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ if and only if it has a run on $x$, that is, a sequence of states $s_0 s_1 s_2 \cdots$ with $s_0$ a start state and a transition from $s_k$ to $s_{k+1}$ reading $x_k$ for every $k$, such that $s_k$ is an accepting state for infinitely many $k$.
nodes.title: Büchi acceptance condition

nodes.summary: For a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states and a decidable start set, this is the set of its start states, viewed as a finite set.
nodes.title: Finite set of start states

nodes.summary: For a nondeterministic Büchi automaton, the transition graph has an edge from a state $s$ to a state $t$ exactly when the automaton has a transition from $s$ to $t$ reading some symbol.
nodes.title: Symbol-forgetting transition graph of a Büchi automaton

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
